why: Both wrapped the same single AsyncOpenAI client and moved the same five call sites, but A's system-level work is deeper and verifiably correct: it labels spend per role inside the migration itself, then fixes the three things that decide whether any of this reaches production — the example config that cannot even import, the shipped default model that Router does not list (so B's deployment routes nothing while B leaves that as an open decision), and the silently discarded browser screenshots plus the PNG media-type 400 that fix exposed — with eight green branches and before/after live measurements for caching, Flex and fallback fall-through. B's proposal set is bolder in places (Switchyard measured at 29x, retiring the boto3 shim, cheap-model-with-escalation anchored on the existing is_stuck detector, and it alone spotted the chart tool's Node subprocess as untracked LLM traffic), but it built less, left the model decision to the operator, and shipped a per-agent branch that fails the outside check on an f-string SyntaxError — the very defect A noticed and repaired in its equivalent change.
A_best: Found and fixed the most expensive invisible bug in the product by testing rather than reading: MULTIMODAL_MODELS silently deleted every base64 screenshot for any model newer than early 2024, so the browser agent — the project's headline feature — was reasoning blind about pages it never saw; enabling it surfaced a second bug (every image announced as image/jpeg while all producers emit PNG, which Anthropic rejects), both proven live on claude-sonnet-5 and claude-haiku-5-5.
B_best: The only report to inventory the chart tool's Node subprocess (chartVisualize.ts:343 building `${baseUrl}/chat/completions`) as real LLM traffic that cannot move because Router serves no Chat Completions endpoint, and the most ambitious correct Router leverage: a measured Switchyard comparison ($0.000109 vs claude-sonnet-5's $0.003184 on a real OpenManus step) paired with an honest refusal to adopt it on n=4 without a quality run, plus retiring app/bedrock.py with its named defects (module-global CURRENT_TOOLUSE_ID, dropped system messages).
A_worst: Treated the chart tool's subprocess call as out of scope entirely — it appears nowhere in the call inventory — so the report claims every LLM call in the codebase goes through app/llm.py when one does not, and the visible improvement set stops short of the boldest structural questions (whether the strong model should take every step at all, or whether the Bedrock shim should exist), which B does raise.
B_worst: Shipped a branch the outside check marks ok:false — the per-agent-llm commit leaves a backslash inside an f-string expression in data_visualization.py that fails to parse on the target Python — and then declined to pick a catalog model for the shipped claude-3-7-sonnet default, so a deployment following the README still sends zero traffic to Router after the whole migration lands.
